do_more: Focus on concrete, quirky physical objects as the central metaphor (mugs, raincoats) rather than abstract brain concepts.
Use active, paradoxical framing in the title (e.g., 'The X Paradox' or 'The X Certainty') to trigger instant curiosity.
Keep the psychological premise grounded in embarrassing everyday micro-failures that Leo and Mia can immediately act out.
Punch up the dialogue humor in the first 3 seconds with a high-stakes disagreement between Leo and Mia.
avoid: Avoid dry, literal titles like 'Why Your Brain Keeps Tabs Open' that sound like a textbook lecture.
Avoid overly complex metaphors like computer tabs or endless cereal aisles that dilute the visual comedy.
Avoid starting skits with setup exposition instead of jumping straight into the comedic argument.
short.title_style: Winning titles use a catchy, specific noun paired with an intriguing abstract noun or outcome (e.g., 'The Mug Paradox', 'The Raincoat Certainty') creating an immediate cognitive itch.
next_tests: Test a title format using 'The [Everyday Object] Effect' to see if object-based paradoxes consistently outperform behavioral concepts.
Test a high-conflict cold open where Leo accuses Mia of a specific psychological fallacy within the first 2 seconds.
